## bd remote

Make this machine a client of another machine's brain.

  brain remote set &lt;ssh-target&gt;   name the brain host (e.g. me@host.ts.net)
  brain remote install            write a wrapper per store in the host's registry
  brain remote status             show the host, reachability, latency, versions
  brain remote disconnect         close the shared ssh connection
  brain remote unset              go back to using local databases

Once a host is set, 'brain …' and every installed store command ('task create',
'inbox list', …) run the same command line on the host over ssh, through the
host's own wrappers, with arguments, stdin, TTY and exit code preserved. The
Dolt server is never reached over the network. BRAIN_REMOTE=off runs a command
locally once; BRAIN_REMOTE_HOST=&lt;target&gt; overrides the configured host. An
exported BEADS_DIR that names a local beads project also runs locally, unforwarded.
A bare 'brain create|update|close|delete|import' runs locally against a .beads
workspace found from the working directory (BEADS_DIR unset), and is refused
rather than forwarded otherwise, so the host's default store never absorbs a
write that named no store; reads and store commands ('task create') forward as
always.

Config: ~/.config/brain/remote.yaml. See docs/brain/REMOTE.md.

```
bd remote [flags]
```

### bd remote disconnect

Close the shared ssh connection (the next call reopens it)

```
bd remote disconnect [flags]
```

### bd remote install

Reads the host's store registry ('brain stores list' there) and writes one
small wrapper per store into --dir (default: the directory of this binary).
Re-run it whenever the host gains a store. It only ever replaces files it
generated itself plus old local-style store wrappers (a sh script that only
exports BEADS_DIR/BD_NAME/… and execs bd), which it replaces after copying them
to &lt;dir&gt;.bak-remote-&lt;timestamp&gt;. Any other file needs --force (also backed up).
It never writes a command called 'bd' or the brain binary, and reports any
wrapper that shadows (or is shadowed by) another command on PATH.

```
bd remote install [flags]
```

**Flags:**

```
      --also strings   Extra command names to install (host wrappers that are not registry stores)
      --bin string     Brain binary the wrappers exec (default: this binary)
      --dir string     Directory for the wrappers (default: this binary's directory)
      --dry-run        Show what would change without writing
      --force          Also replace foreign files (not generated by this command, not a legacy store wrapper); backed up first
      --prune          Remove generated wrappers for stores the host no longer has
```

### bd remote set

Name the brain host (an ssh target such as user@host)

```
bd remote set <ssh-target> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

```
      --bin-dir string   Where the host keeps its wrappers (default $HOME/.local/bin)
      --no-check         Save without contacting the host
```

### bd remote status

Show the configured host, reachability, latency and versions

```
bd remote status [flags]
```

### bd remote unset

Stop forwarding; use local databases again

```
bd remote unset [flags]
```

### bd remote verify

Checks the wrappers in --dir (default: this binary's directory) for every
store in the registry:

  client mode  every wrapper pins BRAIN_REMOTE_STORE='&lt;store&gt;' (no old local
               wrapper left), and no legacy wrapper lingers in the directory;
  every mode   '&lt;store&gt; list --limit 1' returns that store's own id prefix, not
               another store's (e.g. 'status' answering with brain- ids).

On a client the store names come from the host's registry; on the host (no
brain host set) from the local registry, and the pin check is skipped.
Empty stores are reported as 'empty' (prefix unconfirmed), not as failures.

```
bd remote verify [flags]
```

**Flags:**

```
      --dir string         Directory holding the wrappers (default: this binary's directory)
      --timeout duration   Per-store timeout for 'list' (default 1m0s)
```
